headline: 12.7 million children's education disrupted in Bangladesh due to climate change
summary: A UN report reveals that natural disasters are the primary cause of educational losses for millions of Bangladeshi children.
details: A new UN research report by 'Education Cannot Wait' reveals that over 250 million children and adolescents worldwide are seeing their education disrupted by conflict, socio-economic crises, and climate change.

In Bangladesh, approximately 12.7 million children have had their education affected. Out of the total 42.8 million school-aged children in the country, this represents a significant portion of the youth population.

The report highlights that natural disasters are the overwhelming cause of these disruptions in Bangladesh, accounting for 98.1% of the cases, while socio-economic crises contribute to the remaining 1.9%.

Globally, 93 million children have dropped out of school entirely due to these crises. The report notes that 60% of these affected children live in just nine countries, including Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Myanmar, and Nigeria.

Maysa Jalbout, Director of 'Education Cannot Wait', stated that conflict and climate change are reversing educational gains. She emphasized that the report identifies where the most urgent help and investment are needed.

12.7 million children in Bangladesh are losing out on education. The primary cause? Natural disasters.

A new UN research report by 'Education Cannot Wait' reveals that over 250 million children and adolescents worldwide are seeing their education disrupted by conflict, socio-economic crises, and climate change.

In Bangladesh, approximately 12.7 million children have had their education affected. Out of the total 42.8 million school-aged children in the country, this represents a significant portion of the youth population.

The report highlights that natural disasters are the overwhelming cause of these disruptions in Bangladesh, accounting for 98.1% of the cases, while socio-economic crises contribute to the remaining 1.9%.

Globally, 93 million children have dropped out of school entirely due to these crises. The report notes that 60% of these affected children live in just nine countries, including Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Myanmar, and Nigeria.

Maysa Jalbout, Director of 'Education Cannot Wait', stated that conflict and climate change are reversing educational gains. She emphasized that the report identifies where the most urgent help and investment are needed.

headline: Former army officer arrested for alleged attacks on student protesters
summary: The arrest comes amid ongoing investigations into violence during the student-led movement.
details: A former army officer has been arrested in connection with alleged attacks on students during the recent student-led movement.
The arrest was carried out by law enforcement agencies as part of an ongoing investigation into the violence that occurred during the protests.
Authorities are continuing to probe the incidents to identify and hold accountable those involved in the attacks on protesters.
